hooks.command: cmd=$(jq -r ".tool_input.command // \"\""); if printf "%s" "$cmd" | grep -Eq "(^|[;&|] *)(env +[A-Za-z_0-9=]+ +)*gh pr create" && ! printf "%s" "$cmd" | grep -q "BOOK_OK=1"; then printf "%s" "{\"hookSpecificOutput\":{\"hookEventName\":\"PreToolUse\",\"permissionDecision\":\"deny\",\"permissionDecisionReason\":\"Book check gate: before creating this PR, review the branch diff against the chapters in book/ and update any chapter whose material this branch changes (commit the updates so they ride in the PR). If no chapter is affected, tell the user why. Once the check is done, re-run the same command prefixed with: env BOOK_OK=1 (exactly that prefix, at the very start of the command). That re-run triggers one fast gate review, which may block with findings to fix.\"}}"; fi

hooks.prompt: You are the final gate before PR creation in the cocovm Rust workspace. Pre-PR reviews (idiomatic-rust + pr-challenger) have normally already run on this branch, so your job is a fast last-line check, NOT a re-review. Determine the base branch (origin/main if it exists, else main), run git diff $BASE...HEAD --stat first, then read only the riskiest parts of the diff. Look specifically for: accidental stray or generated files committed into the diff; obviously broken logic or invariants in changed code; book/ prose or line-numbered source links the diff makes false; and brand-new behavior with no test at all. Verdict first; PASS is a first-class outcome — do not manufacture findings, do not review style (pre-PR reviews own that), do not re-verify what the compiler, clippy, and the test suite already guarantee, and never request tests that assert a removed feature stays absent. FAIL only for concrete must-fix problems, each as file:line plus one sentence on why it is wrong. Target well under five minutes.
hooks.statusMessage: Gate review of the PR diff
